- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply 0.8–1.2% upward bias for first 7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after 2–3 consecutive peaks), model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
